# Dialect support

Postgres, SQLite and MySQL 8 run the same schemas, changesets, queries and repo calls. This
page lists where they differ. It is generated from each adapter's capability table
(`adapter.capabilities`), so it says what the adapters do.

A query or write that needs a feature the database lacks throws `QueryError`, naming the
feature and the database, when it is compiled: nothing is sent, and nothing is emulated
behind your back. The conformance suites run on every database; a case that needs a
capability the database lacks is skipped, and the skip names the capability.

## Queries

| Feature | Capability | Postgres | SQLite | MySQL 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fullJoin` | `fullJoin` | yes | yes | no |
| `LATERAL` joins (query trees only; no builder method yet) | `lateralJoin` | yes | no | yes |
| `distinct(callback)` (`DISTINCT ON`) | `distinctOn` | yes | no | no |
| `ilike` | `ilike` | yes | as `LIKE`: case-insensitive for ASCII letters only | as `LIKE`: the column's collation decides |
| `nullsFirst()` / `nullsLast()` | `nullsOrder` | yes | yes | no |
| Array columns and array operators | `arrays` | yes | no | no |
| `in(list)` as one array parameter | `arrayParams` | yes | expanded to `in (?, ?, …)` | expanded to `in (?, ?, …)` |
| `jsonb` and its containment operators | `jsonb` | yes | no; JSON is text, read with the JSON functions | no; `json` columns, read with the JSON functions |
| `filter(...)` on an aggregate (`FILTER (WHERE …)`) | `aggregateFilter` | yes | yes | no |
| `withCte(..., { materialized })` | `cteMaterialized` | yes | yes | no |
| A CTE that writes (`updateAll` / `deleteAll` in `withCte`) | `writingCtes` | yes | no | no |
| `intersectAll` / `exceptAll` | `intersectExceptAll` | yes | no | yes |
| `limit` / `offset` from an expression (not only a value or parameter) | `limitExpressions` | yes | yes | no |
| `repo.explain` options (`analyze`, `format`, …) | `explainOptions` | yes | no | yes, except `analyze` with `format: "json"` |

Without the feature:

- `fullJoin` (MySQL 8): Write a `union` of a `leftJoin` and a `rightJoin`.
- `distinct(callback)` (`DISTINCT ON`) (SQLite, MySQL 8): Rank the rows with `rowNumber().over(...)` in a subquery and keep rank 1.
- `nullsFirst()` / `nullsLast()` (MySQL 8): Order by `x.isNull()` first, then by the column.
- Array columns and array operators (SQLite, MySQL 8): Arrays are stored as JSON text (an array of the elements) and read back as arrays; the array operators and `in(arrayExpression)` are refused. Use `t.json()` and JSON functions to query inside them.
- `filter(...)` on an aggregate (`FILTER (WHERE …)`) (MySQL 8): Aggregate a `caseWhen(...)` that is null for the rows to leave out.
- A CTE that writes (`updateAll` / `deleteAll` in `withCte`) (SQLite, MySQL 8): Run the write first, in the same transaction.
- `limit` / `offset` from an expression (not only a value or parameter) (MySQL 8): Compute the number first and pass it as a value.

## Writes

| Feature | Capability | Postgres | SQLite | MySQL 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rows returned from a write; `.returning(...)` on bulk writes | `returning` | yes | yes | no: `insert` and `update` read the row back by its key; bulk writes return counts |
| `onConflict` (upserts) | `onConflict` | yes | yes | yes |
| `onConflict.target` | `conflictTarget` | yes | yes | no: any unique key conflicts (`ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`); leave `target` out |
| `onConflict.target: { constraint }` | `conflictConstraint` | yes | no | no |
| Inserting a row of defaults only | `insertDefaultValues` | yes | yes | yes |
| `insertAll` rows with different fields (`DEFAULT` in `VALUES`) | `defaultInValues` | yes | no | yes |
| Joins in `updateAll` / `deleteAll` | `updateJoin` | yes | no | yes |

Without the feature:

- `insertAll` rows with different fields (`DEFAULT` in `VALUES`) (SQLite): Give every row the same fields, or insert the rows in groups that share them.
- Joins in `updateAll` / `deleteAll` (SQLite): Filter with `where(... in(subquery))` instead of a join.

## Transactions and connections

| Feature | Capability | Postgres | SQLite | MySQL 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nested transactions (savepoints) | `savepoints` | yes | yes | yes |
| `transaction(..., { readOnly: true })` | `readOnlyTransactions` | yes | no | yes |
| `deferrable: true` (serializable, read-only) | `deferrableTransactions` | yes | no | no |
| Serializable transactions fail with a serialization error | `serializationFailures` | yes | no | no: a conflict surfaces as a deadlock (`code: "deadlock"`), also retryable |
| DDL inside a transaction (migrations roll back as a whole) | `ddlTransactions` | yes | yes | no: each DDL statement commits; a migration that fails midway is left half-applied |
| More than one connection | `multipleConnections` | yes | no: one handle, used by one caller at a time; transactions run one after the other | yes |
| Cancelling a running statement (`timeoutMs`, `signal`) | `cancel` | yes | no: a statement runs to its end; `timeoutMs` and `signal` bound the wait for the handle | yes |
| `repo.stream` | `stream` | yes | yes | yes |

## Values and errors

| Feature | Capability | Postgres | SQLite | MySQL 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NaN` and infinities in float columns | `nonFiniteFloats` | yes | no | no |
| `t.decimal()` reads back as written and compares by value (`1.0` = `1.00`) | `exactDecimals` | yes | no: stored as the text given, compared as text | no: the column's scale is fixed (`1.0` reads back as `1.00`) |
| Foreign-key violations name the constraint and the table | `foreignKeyNames` | yes | no: `ConstraintError` has `type: "foreignKey"` and no name | yes |
| Identifiers longer than 64 bytes | `longIdentifiers` | yes, shortened to 63 bytes | yes | no: refused; name a long constraint yourself with `{ name }` |

Without the feature:

- `NaN` and infinities in float columns (SQLite, MySQL 8): Writing one throws `CastError`; store it as null or as text.

## Locks, isolation levels and limits

| | Postgres | SQLite | MySQL 8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Row locks (`lock(...)`) | `FOR UPDATE`, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE NOWAIT`, `FOR SHARE`, `FOR SHARE SKIP LOCKED`, `FOR SHARE NOWAIT`, `FOR KEY SHARE`, `FOR KEY SHARE SKIP LOCKED`, `FOR KEY SHARE NOWAIT` | accepted and not written (one writer at a time) | `FOR UPDATE`, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`, `FOR SHARE`, `FOR SHARE SKIP LOCKED`, `FOR SHARE NOWAIT` |
| Isolation levels | read committed, repeatable read, serializable | none: one writer at a time, and asking for a level is refused | read committed, repeatable read, serializable |
| Parameters per statement | 65,535 | 32,766 | 65,535 |

`insertAll` splits its rows into statements under the parameter limit. A statement that
needs more parameters than the limit (a very long `in` list, say) is refused with
`QueryError` before it is sent.

## Migrations

From the migration table of each dialect (`features`). A migration that uses a feature
the database lacks throws `MigrationError` before anything runs.

| Feature | Feature flag | Postgres | SQLite | MySQL 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tables in a database schema (`createSchema`, `schema` option) | `schemas` | yes | no | yes |
| `createExtension` | `extensions` | yes | no | no |
| `concurrently` index builds and drops | `concurrentIndexes` | yes | no | no |
| Partial indexes (`where`) | `partialIndexes` | yes | yes | no |
| Covering indexes (`include`) | `includeColumns` | yes | no | no |
| Exclusion constraints | `exclusionConstraints` | yes | no | no |
| `cascade` on drops | `dropCascade` | yes | no | no |
| DDL inside a transaction | `ddlTransactions` (capability) | yes | yes | no |
| The runner's lock | `lock` | a lock of the session | a write transaction for the whole run | a lock of the session |

## Constraint names

SQLite reports a unique violation by its columns, not by an index name. The adapter turns
that into the default constraint name (`users_email_key`, or `users_pkey` for the primary
key), so `uniqueConstraint("email")` matches; a custom `name` cannot be matched there,
except for a unique index on an expression, which SQLite reports by its name.

MySQL names the primary key `PRIMARY`; the adapter reports it as `<table>_pkey`. A unique
index created without a name is named after its first column (`email`), not
`users_email_key`: the migrations of this library always name it, and for one created
otherwise, pass its name to `uniqueConstraint(…, { name })`.
